SECOND-PASS CONSUMER REVIEW — AMEND exact off-tree draft SHA-256 59eb12976e3d9bf3114f643fa5b15dcd915796169e0171db56ceeff08840d1c0. The four prior repairs now pass in substance: transactional absent-target publication, opaque extension retention, cross-root closure, and the Tier-1 versus Tier-2 O3 comparison boundary. Four remaining decisions or contradictions should close before durable installation.

1. SOURCE-STAGE OUTCOMES. Section 4.1 makes original bytes and canonical text conditional, and section 10.1 explicitly supports decode failure before canonical text exists. But the section 7.7 wire discussion describes original and canonical as complete artifact references, while section 11 cross-root laws can be read as requiring both in every produced result. The always-present result needs typed source-stage branches such as Produced, Failed, and causally NotAttempted; only Produced branches carry references that must resolve bijectively. Missing fields or placeholder zero-length source identities would repeat the empty-model error.

2. PARTIAL SEMANTIC ARTIFACT POLICY. Sections 4.2 and 7.3 currently forbid semantic_model bytes for every Partial branch. That is not yet a board ruling: the epic says Draft/Partial, and the existing StoryModelCodec deliberately encodes StoryModel at either phantom status and decodes to Draft. Decide explicitly whether Partial may carry an optional canonical draft-model reference plus nonempty gaps, with validation status held only by the result branch and receipt. If the answer is no, state the intentional loss boundary and forbid a parallel draft graph from leaking into generic payloads.

3. MANIFEST-LAST REVERIFICATION. The publication sequence re-reads non-manifest files, then writes manifest.json last and immediately renames. Re-read the exact manifest bytes, compare them with the prepared canonical bytes, decode and validate them, and compute the external BundleId before the atomic commit. Also state that a failure discovered after the commit point cannot be reported as Refused with no final target; the outcome vocabulary must not deny an already-visible committed directory.

4. MIXED VIEW BASIS. Section 8 correctly says ViewBasis is derived and the current cases are not a closed proof, but the illustrative root still carries one optional basis and no heterogeneous-provenance rule. Define a deterministic derivation for mixed admitted roots: either a lossless composite/mixed basis or typed refusal. Add a court showing that precedence or a caller label cannot relabel acquired plus adjudicated or fixture plus acquired material as one purer authority.

One clarity repair: preview.txt may fail independently only if a produced preview.html still contains its complete accessible in-document textual twin. Otherwise the visual report would be Produced while violating section 10.5 and the mission textual-twin law.

Disposition: AMEND before candidate, not block on the overall architecture. No public type-name adoption, dependency ruling, implementation, or landing authority is implied.
